summary: I built SL-044's folder tree in the App only; Core is unchanged. When a scan completes, a virtualized stock WPF TreeView takes the results list's place. It reads the finished ScanResult.Store through a FolderTreeSession that the next scan closes. Each folder's rows are built once, in ChildrenLargestFirst order, the first time it is opened. Each row shows name, on disk, size, a share bar and a one-decimal percentage. Stopped, failed and unreadable endings keep the flat list and show no tree. The hook has a new JSON-logging tree mode that reads what each row's container actually draws. Six new window cases (T-001..T-006) cover every owed row, and C-002, L-003, B-003, B-007 and M-001 now read the tree. `WindowCases.ps1 -Case All` passed all 34 cases. Row 5's cold open of 100,000 files took 64.6-72.4 ms at the default window size and about 106 ms in a 1,000 px window, against a 500 ms limit.

files.why: Holds the finished store for the tree; closed at the next StartScan, so rows WPF keeps (selected item, recycled containers) hold no store (M2). Also records the last open's sort and row-build times for the hook.

One tree row: entry, ChildRow.OnDisk and Share. Name and sizes are read from the store on draw. INotifyPropertyChanged for IsExpanded and Children. A shared constant stand-in row for unopened folders (m4). EnsureChildren builds the rows once in Core's order with a single Children swap.
Share text as Math.Round(share*100,1,AwayFromZero).ToString('F1', CurrentCulture) + ' %' (m2); bar width share x 60 px, with at least 1 px for a nonzero share; sizes through MainWindow.FormatSize.

FolderTree in TopLevelList's cell: IsVirtualizing, Recycling, Pixel scroll, 20 px rows, IsExpanded bound TwoWay, TextBlocks only, named template parts. Column headings; an item template whose header runs to the right edge; Expanded and PreviewKeyDown wiring.

ShowFolderTree on a Completed ending; ClearFolderTree (closes the session) at StartScan. OnFolderExpanded builds rows and re-raises any fault on the dispatcher (m4). OnFolderTreeKeyDown swallows numpad * (M1). LastFolderSortMs and LastFolderBuildMs for the hook.
Schema 1 gains window.FolderTree {visible, actualHeight, inView, realizedRows, fullRows}: layout only, no rows or names (Q-016).

FSA_HOOK_MODE=tree with steps: WALK (breadth-first, BringIndexIntoViewPublic plus a Loaded pass per row, rendered text), RECYCLE, EXPAND (5 timed opens with the sort/build/layout split; refuses the root), MULTIPLY, SELECT+RELEASE (WeakReference taken in a NoInlining helper, GC on the hook thread), GAP (Input probes, window moves), HEIGHT. Logs JSON lines.

Dispatches tree mode; FSA_HOOK_EXPAND may be a path for tree; throw mode logs the tree's state at shutdown; three helpers made internal for TreeMode. Nothing the WindowMutants regexes match was changed.

New cases T-001..T-006 and their helpers (oracle from the built tree, fsutil sparse measurement, Format-Share with AwayFromZero). C-002, L-003, B-003, B-007 and M-001 moved from the flat list to the tree or report.FolderTree. New hook variables registered for cleanup.
Its hard-coded settled-rule count went from 24 to 28 (and 25 to 29) because of the SL-044 entries; otherwise RuleCases C-001 and C-003 fail.

SL-044 Core rule turned into an allow-list over src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs with the correct except paths (m5). Two new no-view-sort rules for *.xaml and MainWindow.xaml.cs (m6). SL-039's 'window never touches the scan store' narrowed with an exception for FolderTree*.cs.
What was settled; what a live tree needs first (Core read path); measurements; the named row-5 remedy (M5); what was found at build.

obligations.how: T-001 checks that the ending is Finished, FolderTree is shown with one root row labelled by the root path, the headings are shown and TopLevelList is not. C-002 now reads the tree root's 150 children through tree mode (WALK=1), where it used to read topLevel. Passed.

T-001's size_&_order folder holds sparse.bin (1 MiB in bytes, 64 KiB on disk), dense.bin (128 KiB) and my_file&co.bin (12 KiB). The drawn order is dense, sparse, my_file. Every folder's children are also checked non-increasing by on-disk size against the case's own oracle. Passed.

T-001 checks deep\mid\low (three levels deep), chain (only a folder chain, no files of its own) and the root. The root's size equals everything below it and the sum of its drawn rows. Every folder's raw and drawn totals match the oracle built from the files the case wrote. Passed.

T-001's 'empty' folder is drawn with no expander, 0 bytes and a 0.0 % share. Unreadable folders also get no expander and a 'could not be opened' note, which the real-input run showed for C:\Program Files\WindowsApps. Passed.

T-001 creates a junction (j), a folder symlink (sd) and a file symlink (sf) into a folder outside the root holding 1 MiB. Each is drawn with no expander, 0 bytes and 'link, not followed', and none of the outside bytes appear in any total. Passed; Developer Mode symlinks were created unelevated.

T-001's zeros folder holds three 0-byte files under a parent with 0 on disk. Each child is drawn as '0.0 %' with a bar whose laid-out width is exactly 0 (Core's Share 0; the formatter does no division). Three files rather than 100,000, as the M4 fix specified. Passed.

T-001 checks thirds (1/3 x3), twothirds (1/3 and 2/3), sixteenths (1/16 = 6.25 drawn as 6.3 %, 15/16 = 93.75 drawn as 93.8 %) and tiny (4 KiB under 8 MiB drawn as '0.0 %' with a 1 px bar, not empty). The expected values use [math]::Round(x,1,AwayFromZero) and F1 in the current culture. Passed.
T-001 checks the rendered NameText of 'size_&_order', 'my_file&co.bin' and a 149-character name. Each is drawn exactly as written, on a 20 px row that stays one line (trimmed). Passed.

T-003 uses 100,000 files in big, a child of the root: 50 distinct 4 KiB multiples, the rest empty. Five opens at the default window size and five in a 1,000 px window, each timed from IsExpanded on the container to the first ContextIdle pass with the first child's row built. Cold opens took 64.6-72.4 ms and about 106 ms; warm opens 0.9-3.7 ms. 4 and 14 rows were built (virtualization on), and the first row was the 200 KiB file. Passed.

T-002 opens many (60 folders; 1,410 px of rows in a 39 px viewport), then opens f02 (third from the end). It scrolls to the end and back twice, then closes and reopens many. Only f02 is open, both by node state and as drawn on its own row; order, sizes and f02's child are unchanged. Passed.

T-004 opens a 3,000-row folder five times (leaving it open) and selects and focuses a row three levels deep. It then starts a scan of a second root through the window's own StartScan. The first store's WeakReference was dead while the second scan was still running (asserted) and again after it ended. The tree then showed only the new root. Passed.

T-006 covers three endings. Stop mid-scan: the report has FolderTree.visible false and the list in view with its final snapshot. A UI-thread fault mid-scan: exit 70, and the hook logs tree=False treeItems=0 at shutdown (the tree is now captured before the fault, after a first version passed vacuously). A missing root: no tree. L-003 also checks missing and relative roots show no tree. Passed.

T-005 scans 100,000 files and 20,000 folders while the hook moves and resizes the window every 50 ms (23 moves). It then covers the hand-off, one open of big and a second scan over the open tree, probing the UI thread at Input priority every 50 ms. The longest wait was 47 ms; per-phase p95 was 0.5-30 ms (limits: 1,000 ms max, 200 ms p95). Passed.

FolderTree PreviewKeyDown marks Key.Multiply handled. T-003's multiply step closes every folder, selects and focuses the root row and raises PreviewKeyDown then KeyDown for Multiply: previewHandled true, 0 folders opened. A hand-run mutant with the handler unwired opened 9 rows below the root, so the check can fail.

Rows hold a FolderTreeSession, never the store, and StartScan closes it. The release case selects and focuses a depth-3 row first, waits a ContextIdle pass, and takes the WeakReference in a [MethodImpl(NoInlining)] helper; GC runs on the hook thread. The other store-derived lists were already cleared at StartScan (the critique's own note), so no ShownScan holder was added. T-004 passed.

For every row the hook re-resolves the index path from the tree. Each level is realized through the parent's items panel with VirtualizingPanel.BringIndexIntoViewPublic, a Loaded-priority pass follows, and the container is read before the next row. T-001 (36 rows), C-002 (151 rows) and the real run (648 rows) had 0 unrendered rows.

Case A (T-001) has the zeros folder (three 0-byte files), thirds (3 x 4 KiB), twothirds (16+32 KiB), sixteenths and tiny (8 MiB + 4 KiB). FSA_HOOK_RECYCLE (T-002) opens a low child, scrolls away and back, closes and reopens its parent, and logs every child's node and container state and its order.

The hook logs open 1's sortMs, buildMs and layoutMs (the rest), for example 46.6 / 8.6 / 16.3 ms. docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md names the remedy that shortens the measured interval: build rows only for the indexes WPF asks for, through a read-only list over ChildRow[]. It states that a worker thread is only a responsiveness measure. Per O-015's answer, no worker was built.

The template's elements have x:Names (NameText, NoteText, OnDiskText, SizeText, ShareText, ShareTrack, ShareBar). The hook reads them through PART_Header's ContentTemplate.FindName and logs rendered.barActualWidth and barTrackWidth. T-001 asserts the bar within 1 px of share x 60, a width of 0 for a zero share, and a track of 60 px shown except on the root.

FolderTreeRowText.Share uses Math.Round(share*100,1,MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).ToString('F1', CurrentCulture). WindowCases' Format-Share uses [math]::Round(x,1,[MidpointRounding]::AwayFromZero) with F1. Case A contains 1/16 (6.25 drawn as 6.3 %) and 15/16 (93.75 drawn as 93.8 %). Passed.

Sparse file only (no compression): 64 KiB of data at 256 KiB in a 1 MiB file. Its allocation is measured with fsutil sparse queryrange, which runs unelevated, and ancestors' totals and shares come from that measurement. Sibling folder totals are distinct. The listing could not be read without interop, so the fixture writes data before extending the file, which keeps the directory entry current. Length-first left the entry at 0 and the store charged 0, which T-001 caught; see deviations and follow-ups.

FolderTreeNode.IsExpanded only records state. Rows are built in MainWindow.OnFolderExpanded (the TreeViewItem.Expanded routed event), which catches any exception and re-raises it on the dispatcher at Send priority, because the expander click also reaches it through a binding. The shared stand-in row's session holds no store, so its getters return constants.

The Core rule is now an allow-list: files src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs, pattern \bScanStore\b, except Store/ScanStore*.cs, Scanning/Scanner.cs, Scanning/ScanResult.cs, TopLevelTracker.cs and Analysis/LargestFiles.cs. The wrong except path src/FsAnalyser.Core/ScanResult.cs was fixed. A regex run over the 12 remaining Core files found no match.

Added settled rules over src/FsAnalyser.App/*.xaml and src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs forbidding SortDescriptions|CollectionViewSource|IsLiveSorting. Grep confirmed the flat list sorts with Array.Sort in code, so no existing code moved. Both rules match nothing.

The 100k folder is big, a child of the root; ExpandTimed logs an error if FSA_HOOK_EXPAND resolves to the root. 'Cold' now means the rows are built on that open (the root's expand at completion already JITs the path) and is asserted only for open 1. Per the decision, row 6's hand-off and new-scan-over-a-large-tree go to a hook-driven gap case (T-005), not an extended StallRig.

tests.note: 0 warnings, 0 errors. The App and the hook also built on their own with 0 warnings.

tests.note: 240 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, including ArchitectureRulesTests and RuleCopiesAgreeTests.

Published the single-file exe and built the hook. PASSED all 34 cases: C-001..C-014, O-016, L-001..L-003, B-001..B-008, V-001, P-001, T-001..T-006. N-001..N-004 were NOT RUN (they change SMB mappings; person-run with -IncludeNetwork). B-007 at the window's minimum size: FolderTree 43 px, 1 full row.

First run: the store charged sparse.bin 0 bytes on disk while fsutil sparse queryrange reported 64 KiB allocated (a stale directory entry for a length-first sparse write; SizeProbe trusts the listing for sparse files). The fixture now writes data before extending; the re-run and the All run passed. Recorded as a Core follow-up.

One intermediate run failed only on my own precondition (a 1,000 px window would give the tree 300 px; it gives 134 px because of SL-040's 3:1 split). Changed to 'more than twice the default viewport'; passed in the All run: cold 72.4 ms default, 106.4 ms tall.
Re-run after lengthening the scan (20,000 folders) and moving the window every 50 ms. The All run had exactly 3 moves against a floor of 3; now 23 moves. Longest UI wait 47 ms.
H-001 and H-002 pass with the changed hook (Run validation, throw-mode shutdown line).
AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 28 settled entries, in both shells.
Includes the appended-entry shape at 29 settled entries.
rules-parity: AGREE. The engine's Fitness check was not available to me. I ran each touched settled rule's patterns over its glob by hand: all clean.

tests.command: published mutant (scratch copy with PreviewKeyDown unwired) under FSA_HOOK_MODE=tree FSA_HOOK_MULTIPLY=1 on a small nested temp tree
tests.note: Hand-run proof that T-003's key check can fail. The mutant logged previewHandled=false and expandedBeyondRoot=9; the real exe logged previewHandled=true and 0. Scratch deleted.

Real input through the real entry point: exit 0 after 6 s. 648 rows walked, all drawn; the root (31.8 GB on disk) equals the sum of its 53 rows in both columns; 0 order violations; drawn shares equal computed ones. WindowsApps is noted 'could not be opened'. Top row: NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit, 4.8 GB, 15.1 %.

deviations: The TreeViewItem container template is replaced (BasedOn the stock style, so its virtualization triggers stay). The stock Aero2 template sizes the header column to its content, so figures docked to the right edge could not line up across depths as the design states. The copy keeps the stock parts and names (Expander, Bd, PART_Header, ItemsHost) and triggers, and only lets the header span to the tree's right edge. The TreeView, its panel and the measured virtualization settings are stock.

--report schema 1 gains window.FolderTree {visible, actualHeight, inView, realizedRows, fullRows}; the design said the report stays unchanged. Without it, B-003, B-007 and L-003 would have nothing to check once the tree replaces TopLevelList after a completed scan (in view, a full row at the window's minimum size). It holds layout only, no row names or figures, so Q-016 holds; the contract already allows added keys.

SL-039's settled rule 'the window never touches the scan store' is narrowed with except_files src/FsAnalyser.App/FolderTree*.cs rather than left as is. The design never mentioned it, yet its FolderTreeNode must name ScanStore, which that rule forbids. SL-039's own doc says the tree slice changes it on purpose; the new Core rule is what keeps a live store out of reach.

For the sparse sibling (m3), the oracle is fsutil sparse queryrange's allocated ranges, not the directory-listing AllocationSize the decision preferred. The listing cannot be read from PowerShell without adding interop to a test script. The fixture writes data before extending the file, which I measured keeps the directory entry equal to the allocation; if they ever diverge, T-001 fails by name, as its first run did.

A nonzero share draws a bar of at least 1 px (design: share x 60). A share like 4 KiB of 8 MiB would otherwise draw 0.03 px, an empty bar, which C-007 says must not happen. The floor stays inside m1's 1 px tolerance.

The hook's tree mode has steps and variables the design did not name: FSA_HOOK_WALK, RECYCLE, MULTIPLY, SELECT, GAP and HEIGHT, next to the designed EXPAND and RELEASE. The accepted critique fixes (M1, M2, M4c, m7) each required a step with no variable given. HEIGHT was added so row 5 is also timed with a realistic number of rows on screen.
not_built: The design's Case D re-run of the StallRig network cases (N-001..N-004) on this build. They create and remove SMB client mappings on this machine, which I may not change, and the m7 decision moved row 6's new steps into a hook-driven case (T-005). The person's network pass is now stale (MainWindow.xaml(.cs), the hook and WindowCases.ps1 are on the staleness list).
follow_ups: Core counting finding: a sparse file written length-first (extended, then data written into the hole) keeps AllocationSize 0 in its directory entry while NTFS has 64 KiB allocated. Seen here also after a rename and after a length-changing reopen; data-first entries were current. SizeProbe trusts the listing for sparse files, so the store charged 3 of 4 such files 0 bytes on disk. That touches the 'space it actually takes on disk' counting rule and belongs to a scanner slice (e.g. probe sparse files whose listing says 0 allocated).

At the default 880x620 window the tree gets a 39 px viewport (about two rows), 43 px at the minimum size, and 134 px in a 1,000 px window. It keeps SL-040's quarter of the height beside the outcome panel. Revisit SL-040's 3:1 split or the default size now that the tree is the main result.
Person-run network pass: WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork plus Core.Tests with Network=SMB-LOOPBACK, because this slice makes the last pass stale.

Re-measure the 1 GiB budget end to end with the as-built tree. The go spike used a stand-in tree layer. Include a drive-scale scan, a large folder opened, and a second scan started over it, to confirm one store in memory at scale (T-004 proves collectability on small stores).

Add WindowMutants entries for the new cases so their ability to fail is re-provable. Suggested: the numpad * handler unwired (checked by hand this build), IsExpanded not bound to the row (T-002), and rows holding the store instead of the session (T-004).

When a live tree is built on a Core read path (per-folder snapshots or seqlock/epoch), retire TopLevelTracker and lift the 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore' rule on purpose, as docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md records.
